[Feature]: support signal in waitFor* APIs

### 🚀 Feature Request

Many Playwright ⁠`waitFor*` APIs support a ⁠timeout option, which works well for fixed upper bounds. A complementary capability would be support for ⁠AbortSignal, so callers can cancel an in-flight wait based on external application state.


### Example

A consistent API shape could look like this wherever ⁠timeout is already supported:
```ts
await locator.waitFor({
  state: 'visible',
  timeout: 30_000,
  signal,
});

await page.waitForURL('**/dashboard', {
```

### Motivation

This would make Playwright waiting APIs easier to compose with:

- shared cancellation across multiple concurrent operations
- higher-level test orchestration
- user-defined deadlines and cascading cancellation
- integration with standard Web Platform and Node.js cancellation patterns

[Feature]: Configurable default grouping for the HTML report ("Merge files" as a default)

### 🚀 Feature Request

Let the HTML reporter's grouping default be set at report-generation time (via config, and/or a URL param), so a report can open already grouped by `describe`, i.e. the equivalent of the "Merge files" toggle being on, without each viewer flipping it by hand.

```ts
// playwright.config.ts
reporter: [['html', { groupBy: 'suite' }]]
```

### Motivation

I have a monorepo where a lot of tests are generated inside a single shared spec file, and each unit is wrapped in `test.describe('@scope/<package>')`. In the merged HTML report every test collapses under that one file header, so I can't tell which package a failure belongs to at a glance.

The "Merge files" option (from #38870) already does exactly the grouping I want: it groups by `describe`, and the group header becomes my `@scope/<package>`. The catch is that it's a per-viewer setting stored in `localStorage['mergeFiles']`, so:

- CI-published reports always open ungrouped, and every person has to know about and click "Merge files".
- It can't be shared via a link (it's a stored setting, not a URL param).
- There's no way to bake the default into the report we publish as an artifact.

### What I'm asking for

A supported way to set the default grouping when the report is generated, e.g. an `HtmlReporterOptions` field (`groupBy: 'file' | 'suite'`, defaulting to `'file'` for back-compat), threaded into the report so it opens grouped. A URL param would be a nice bonus for sharing. The per-viewer toggle would still override it.

The plumbing looks mostly there already: `createMergedFilesModel` in `reportView.tsx` groups by `test.path[0]`, gated behind `useSetting('mergeFiles', ...)`. This would let the generated report seed that default.

(Note: #38870 was closed into #21202, which is broader metadata filtering/grouping. This is narrower, just making the existing "Merge files" grouping configurable as a default, so I'm filing separately. Happy to have it folded in if you'd prefer.)

[Feature]: Expose recorded ResourceTiming on APIResponse (parity with Request.timing())

### 🚀 Feature Request

Browser-originated requests expose detailed network phase timings via [`Request.timing()`](https://playwright.dev/docs/api/class-request#request-timing) (DNS, connect, TLS, TTFB, receive). Requests made through `APIRequestContext` (`request.get/post/...`, `fetch`) return an `APIResponse` that has no equivalent — the only way to get any timing today is to wall-clock the call in userland, which yields a single opaque total.

I'd like to propose exposing the per-phase `ResourceTiming` on `APIResponse`, **read-only**, mirroring `Request.timing()`.

### Why this is a thin change, not a new capability

Playwright **already collects and maintains these exact timings** for `APIRequestContext` — they were added in #32613 (merged) and recorded into the HAR/trace (the trace viewer already shows the duration), and proxy edge cases have since been fixed (#32855). So the data already exists in memory; this request is only to surface it through the public API instead of requiring users to parse trace/HAR artifacts.

A previous PR (#32647) implemented exactly this but was closed with the rationale that "Playwright isn't a network performance testing tool." Respectfully, I'd push back on two points:

1. This isn't about load/performance testing — it's **diagnostic parity** with browser requests, which already expose `timing()`.
2. "Rough timings can be measured in userland" only holds for *total* time. The phase breakdown requires socket-level events (`lookup` / `connect` / `secureConnect` / `response`) on the connection Playwright owns inside `fetch.ts`, including redirect and proxy handling — userland has no access to it. #32647 itself surfaced the SOCKS/HTTP-proxy `connect` timing bug fixed in #32855, which no userland wrapper could have measured correctly.

### Example

```ts
const response = await request.get('https://api.example.com/orders');
console.log(response.timing());
// { startTime, domainLookupStart, domainLookupEnd, connectStart,
//   secureConnectionStart, connectEnd, requestStart, responseStart, responseEnd }
```

The shape would be identical to `Request.timing()`, so there are no new concepts to learn. It could also be gated behind the existing `omitTiming` option to stay opt-out.

### Motivation / use cases

- **Debugging slow or flaky API tests** in CI: knowing whether latency came from DNS, TLS handshake, or the server, instead of one aggregate number.
- **Synthetic monitoring built on Playwright** (e.g. Elastic Synthetics, Checkly) that runs browser and API checks side by side and needs consistent network fields across both. Downstream context: elastic/synthetics#997.

### Prior art / recurring demand

- #19621 — "Is there a way to return an api request response time?" (👍 9); would have been closed by #32647
- #34992 — "Add elapsed time and method name to APIResponse" (👍 3); closed as stale
- #32647 — implemented `APIResponse.timing()`; closed unmerged
- #32613 — records these timings into HAR (merged) — the data source this proposal would expose
- #16239 — access request headers/body/method on API requests (👍 33) — related "surface request/response internals" theme

Happy to help revive #32647 or open a fresh PR if the team is open to a read-only accessor over the already-recorded timings. Thanks for considering!

[Feature] Locks to avoid concurrent runs of specific tests

Errors due to the concurrent runs is a common issue in test automation.
Currently there is no support for locks to avoid this in playwright and the tests must be run sequential, as far as i can tell.
Usually only a small set of tests will require lock, but the test execution is significant slower sequentially.

It is also not possible to implement them outside playwirght for several reasons:
- using a locking mechanism in the test / beforeEach is not possible due to the timeout of the test method
- using a fixture with a custom timeout would be an option, but with differen locks i need different fixtures 
In both options the workers will be blocked until the lock is aquired and we might end in a deadlock if multiple locks are needed.

Playwirght could support locks on test level by adding options to the test(title, callback) method with a list of named locks.
The excution of the test will be block until no other test is currently using these locks. To avoid deadlocks the usage of locks could be limited to not allow nested locks.

`test("call the external interface", (page) => { page... }, { locks: ["LegacySystem"]});`

see: https://github.com/microsoft/playwright/releases/tag/v1.31.0

edit: actually they probably wont work since a single failure in the dependency will prevent running the second project. 
At that point I'd say its probably best to just run two separate projects and have them write to the same directory for the HTML report if thats a need.

Looks like a duplicate of https://github.com/microsoft/playwright/issues/14084 to me.

The other one is per test, this one is about more dynamic locks.

Could you let us know about your use-case? We usually recommend putting critical things in the same file, since we don't do any parallelise there (except fullyParallel is true).

@mxschmitt sure, here are our current and future use-cases as far i can tell for now.

1. We need to increment numbers, earch number can only be used once.
    a) read the latest number
    b) fill the UI with the latest number + 1 and other infos, this takes about 40s
    c) submit the form -> only one test will pass
 
2. We need to do UI operations calling external interfaces to other applications.
    If this interface is called concurrently it is locked, it is not desinged for concurrent uses.

3. (future) Integrate hardware into the process and trigger actions on it. We can only trigger one by one to not disturb each others (e.g. due the reset of the hardware before starting the actual test), be able to assign the logs / generate data to a test run.

We might workaround for 1. and 2. by using different users for earch worker (based on the worker index?), but they will use the same data. So we probably must use different data for each worker, but then we need to get the base data maintained in the external applications too. This approach won't scale if we need more workers in the future.

> We might workaround for 1. and 2. by using different users for earch worker (based on the worker index?), but they will use the same data. 

Can you elaborate on what is wrong with using the same data for each of the test users running in parallel?

> If this interface is called concurrently it is locked, it is not desinged for concurrent uses.

If the interface is not designed for concurrent use you'd better run your tests in serial mode (or have a unique user per parallel worker). Why is it not an option for you? As far as I understand, you want to serialize calls to the service rather than entire tests and this would be outside of playwright scope.

I think i need to explain where the concurrency is comming from, this is done to reduce the testing time with different browsers. fullyParallel is false, workers is 3 and projects is 3 (one project for each browser).
Each worker will process the tests serial, but the different browsers will all start at the same test, following the same order of tests. So we need a locking between the workers (in this case browsers) and not inside one worker.

> Can you elaborate on what is wrong with using the same data for each of the test users running in parallel?

We cannot check the processing is correct for each test run, if the test runs will concurrently overwrite the results.

> If this interface is called concurrently it is locked, it is not desinged for concurrent uses.

this is what is currently happening on the time line, the tests before the critical area are taking different amount of time, so we will not hit the test at the same time, but still while another browser is running:
00:08:02 Chrome - will upload data
00:09:10 Firefox- will upload data
00:08:03 Chrome - data is processing
00:09:13 Firefox - upload failed / due to Chrome data is processing
00:11:00 Chrome - data is processed
00:11:01 Chrome - check the data

Serializing the single calls to the service will not ensure the "check the data" step will pass, a different browser might have overwritten the data in the mean time, so we would need to lock until the complete test is done.

Adding another use case here. 

I'm testing a Call Center webRTC application, in which some actions needs to be evaluated before / during / after a call is placed. Of course users can't be  active on 2 calls at the same (caller and callee and supervisor). 

Creating 1 set of users per test isn't viable either ( would be 3 users per test X number of context [local, ci, regression, healthcheck, smoketests] X environments [local, dev, staging, nightly, live] X each browsers we need to support [chrome, ff, webkit]

Most tests that do not involve placing calls could be fully parallel and it wouldn't be an issue, however, anything that has to place a call cannot be executed in that fashion.

As mentioned above, using dependencies wouldn't really help as a single failure would prevent the subsequent project to run.

Adding Yet Another Use Case

I am currently testing a document management system that is structured into multiple modules. We designed our test structure to mirror the organization of the modules in our project, ensuring that each functionality has its own dedicated test file. However, we are facing a challenge: our modules sometimes modify or utilize the global settings of the system, leading to interference between tests.

Our current solution is to consolidate all these tests into a single test file. This approach has several drawbacks, including the need to increase our global timeout due to the sheer number of tests, even when using test.slow().

Another example involves our Statistics Module. In our system, users can track statistics such as the number of logins or document uploads over a specific time period. The page for activating tracking and the page for viewing the tracked data are two distinct modules, yet they must reside in the same test file.

While it is possible to refactor our teststructure so that all interfering tests are grouped together, this would not only be confusing and unintuitive but also inefficient in many cases. For instance, consider three tests: A, B, and C. Tests A and B interfere with each other, as do tests B and C. Without a locking mechanism, I would be forced to place all three tests in one test file, even though tests A and C could run in parallel without any issues.

I have a single test that uses some canned data, modifies that data, and then resets the data. I want this test to run in multiple browsers, and have most of the tests in the suite run in parallel. But if a firefox worker and a chrome worker both run this test at the same time, the state can get mangled.

Options to solve this:
- Create one dataset for each project: more data to track
- Separate the test runners to run this test in each project sequentially, and other runs in parallel: more complicated configuration to maintain
- Run all tests sequentially: slow
- Put each browser case for this test in a single file so that file is run sequentially: odd special case, and some code reuse. (Probably how I'm going to handle it without this locking mechanism)

A simpler method would be if a test case could be given a lock, and the playwright test worker would skip any tests that are currently locked.

It's not that bad. Here's my tsconfig:
```
    projects: [
        {
            name: 'chromium',
            grepInvert: /firefox|webkit/,
            use: {...devices['Desktop Chrome']},
        },

        {
            name: 'firefox',
            grepInvert: /chromium|webkit/,
            use: {...devices['Desktop Firefox']},
        },

        {
            name: 'webkit',
            grepInvert: /firefox|chromium/,
            use: {...devices['Desktop Safari']},
        },
    ],
```

Then in my test file:
```
test(
    'test1 -chromium',
    {tag: '@chromium'},
    actual_test_function
);

test(
    'test1 -webkit',
    {tag: '@webkit'},
    actual_test_function
);

test(
    'test1 -firefox',
    {tag: '@firefox'},
    actual_test_function
);
```

In the rare case I have tests I only want to run in a specific browser I've already set up a mechanism for it so that's a plus. I'm not sure if this helps with other use cases for a lock.

Any chance this will be considered to be implemented?

On my end I gave up waiting, ended up creating a resource lock service, tests requests a lockable resource, service either accept of denies the lock according to availability. 

Computing the resource to request is the test's responsibility, service is as "dumb" as it can be.

[CLI]: Add a CLI option to append a reporter without replacing configured reporters

### What's going on?

## Feature request

Please add a supported way to append a reporter for the current Playwright test run without replacing the reporters already configured in `playwright.config`.

For example:

```bash
npx playwright test --append-reporter=./custom-reporter.js
```

## Current behaviour

The existing `--reporter` CLI option replaces the reporters configured in the Playwright configuration file.

For example, a project may already use several reporters:

* HTML
* Allure
* JUnit
* Monocart
* One or more custom reporters

An external tool currently cannot add its own reporter at runtime without disabling or reconstructing the project's existing reporter configuration.

## Use case

IDE integrations, CI observability tools may need access to structured Playwright lifecycle events, including:

* Total tests
* Completed tests
* Passed tests
* Failed tests
* Skipped tests
* Currently running tests
* Retry information
* Worker information
* Project information

Parsing terminal output is unreliable and may break when Playwright changes its output format.

A Playwright reporter is the appropriate structured integration point, but there is currently no supported append-only runtime option.

## Desired behaviour

A CLI option such as:

```bash
npx playwright test --append-reporter=./custom-reporter.js
```

should:

* Preserve all reporters configured in `playwright.config`
* Add the supplied reporter only for the current test run
* Support custom reporter options where possible
* Work when a custom configuration path is provided
* Preserve existing HTML, Allure, JUnit, JSON, Monocart, and custom reporters
* Avoid modifying the user's configuration file

For example:

```bash
npx playwright test \
  --config=./configs/playwright.config.ts \
  --append-reporter=./custom-reporter.js
```

A supported public programmatic API or environment-variable-based solution would also address this use case.

## Alternatives considered

### `--reporter`

The existing option replaces the configured reporters instead of appending another reporter.

### Temporary configuration files

Generating a temporary configuration file may:

* Break relative paths
* Affect configuration imports
* Require duplicating or dynamically loading the existing configuration
* Leave temporary files behind when execution terminates unexpectedly

### Editing the user's configuration

This is intrusive and may create unwanted source-control changes or conflicts.

### Parsing terminal output

Terminal output is intended for humans and is not a stable structured interface.

### Using Playwright internals

Internal APIs are undocumented and may change between Playwright versions.

## Additional context

The Playwright reporter API already exposes the structured test lifecycle events required by external tools.

The missing capability is a supported way for external tooling to temporarily attach an additional reporter while preserving the project's existing reporter configuration.

[CLI]: `upload` rejects a second file although it advertises "one or multiple files"

### What's going on?

`playwright-cli upload` takes only one path, but its description, its argument description and the tool behind it all say it takes several.

```
$ playwright-cli click 'css=input[type=file][multiple]'   # chooser opens
$ playwright-cli upload /tmp/front.txt /tmp/back.txt
error: too many arguments: expected 1, received 2

playwright-cli upload <file>

Upload one or multiple files

Arguments:
  <file>                      the absolute paths to the files to upload
```

Three layers disagree and only the CLI declaration is wrong. `browser_file_upload` takes `paths: z.array(z.string()).optional()` ("Can be single file or multiple files"), the description says "Upload one or multiple files", the argument is described in the plural, but `cli-daemon/commands.ts` binds one string and wraps it:

```ts
args: z.object({
  file: z.string().describe('The absolute paths to the files to upload'),
}),
toolName: 'browser_file_upload',
toolParams: ({ file }) => ({ paths: [file] }),
```

I patched the generated bundle locally to check nothing else is in the way. It is not: with the declaration widened, three paths arrive as one `paths` array and the page gets a single `change` event with all three files (`changes=1 count=3`). The arity cap lives in two places, `validateArgs` in `cli-client/program.ts` and `parseCommand` in `cli-daemon/command.ts`.

Calling `upload` once per file is not a workaround. Plenty of pages consume the first selection and remove the chooser, so the second call has nothing to attach to. For an ID document front and back the only way out today is merging the pages into a temporary PDF, which changes the file type the site receives.

Two shapes look reasonable, and I verified both end to end against the bundle:

1. **Variadic positional**, `upload <files...>`: make the last positional absorb the remaining arguments when its schema accepts an array, and declare `files: stringArrayArg`. This is what the current description already promises. Other commands keep their arity error (`mousemove 1 2 3` still says `expected 2, received 3`). One rough edge: a bare `upload` then reports `'files' argument: Invalid input` instead of `expected string, received undefined`, because `stringArrayArg` is a union.
2. **Repeatable `--path`**, exactly like `drop`: no machinery change, contained to `commands.ts`, fully backwards compatible, but it reads oddly for a command whose entire subject is files.

I lean towards 1 and it looks like the same class of fix as #40784, which added `stringArrayArg` for the mirror-image problem. Happy to send a PR for whichever shape you want.

### Version

@playwright/cli 0.1.17 (also 0.1.15; declaration unchanged on `main`)

[Bug]: Browser download retries do not reach IPv4 after an IPv6 TLS timeout

### Version

1.62.1

### Steps to reproduce

Minimal reproduction: https://github.com/martinblech/playwright-ipv6-tls-fallback-repro

1. Clone the repository.
2. Run `npm ci`.
3. Run `npx playwright --version` (it prints `Version 1.62.1`).
4. Run `npm test`.

The repository uses only Node built-ins and `playwright@1.62.1`. It runs the real Playwright browser installer against local loopback listeners, so it does not contact the Playwright CDN or download a browser.

`npm test` runs two cases on the same installer code path:

1. **Control:** the IPv4 listener at `127.0.0.1` completes HTTPS, while nothing accepts IPv6 TCP. Playwright reaches IPv4. The listener deliberately returns HTTP 404 because this case tests address-family reachability, not archive contents.
2. **Reproduction:** the same IPv4 HTTPS listener remains available, while a listener at `::1` accepts TCP and deliberately never completes TLS. Playwright makes five IPv6 TCP connections, reports five download timeouts, and never reaches IPv4.

The script points `PLAYWRIGHT_DOWNLOAD_HOST` at `https://localhost:<random-port>`, clears proxy variables for the installer child process, uses a fresh `PLAYWRIGHT_BROWSERS_PATH`, and sets `PLAYWRIGHT_DOWNLOAD_CONNECTION_TIMEOUT=1000` only to shorten the deterministic wait.

### Expected behavior

When IPv6 accepts TCP but cannot establish HTTPS, while a resolved IPv4 address can establish HTTPS, at least one of the browser installer's retries should reach IPv4 instead of every retry selecting the same stalled IPv6 route.

I do not have a preference about whether fallback happens within the same attempt or on a later retry.

### Actual behavior

The control confirms that the local IPv4 HTTPS endpoint is reachable by the installer:

```text
IPv6 TCP connections accepted: 0
IPv4 HTTPS requests received: 5
Playwright installer exit code: 1
Playwright timeout errors: 0
CONTROL PASSED: Playwright reached IPv4 when IPv6 TCP failed.
```

With IPv6 accepting TCP but stalling TLS, every installer attempt times out and IPv4 receives no requests:

```text
Error: Request to https://localhost:<port>/builds/... timed out after 1000ms
...
IPv6 TCP connections accepted: 5
IPv4 HTTPS requests received: 0
Playwright installer exit code: 1
Playwright timeout errors: 5
BUG REPRODUCED: IPv6 accepted TCP but stalled TLS; Playwright did not reach working IPv4.
```

I reproduced the same behavior on macOS/arm64 with Node 26.7.0 and in a clean Debian 12/arm64 container with Node 22.23.2.

### Additional context

This arose from a real browser installation failure, not only from source inspection. I reproduced the CDN failure in a throwaway npm project using `playwright@1.62.1`, Node 24.2.0, a fresh browser cache, the default 30-second timeout, no `NODE_OPTIONS`, and no HTTP(S) or SOCKS proxy. The installer made five download attempts to the same CDN URL; every attempt timed out after 30000ms, and installation exited with code 1. The same result occurs with Node 26.

On that network, the exact CDN URL produces these direct controls:

```text
family=IPv4 status=307 tcp=0.016493s tls=0.048759s total=0.061296s
family=IPv6 status=000 tcp=0.083410s tls=0.000000s total=5.004128s
curl: (28) SSL connection timeout
```

The nonzero IPv6 TCP time and absent TLS completion match a verbose trace in which TCP connects, a TLS exchange begins, and the handshake does not complete. IPv6 HTTPS to unrelated hosts and to the eventual Google Storage redirect target succeeds from the same machine. I cannot determine from one network whether the underlying TLS stall is caused by the local router, ISP/peering path, or remote CDN path. I am not claiming that Playwright causes that network condition, or that the localhost reproduction duplicates the CDN's TLS packets; it reproduces the relevant failure class in which TCP connects but HTTPS never becomes usable.

The behavior I am reporting is that Playwright's five download retries do not use the available IPv4 path. This is not a request for a global IPv4-only mode.

One source observation that appears consistent with the reproduction: in [`happyEyeballs.ts` for 1.62.1](https://github.com/microsoft/playwright/blob/v1.62.1/packages/utils/happyEyeballs.ts#L131-L172), the TLS path resolves an address attempt on the socket's `connect` event, after which the other sockets are destroyed. This happens before `secureConnect`. [`httpRequest`](https://github.com/microsoft/playwright/blob/v1.62.1/packages/utils/network.ts#L46-L95) uses this agent for HTTPS. Playwright Extension: only one MCP client connection is supported at a time

### Context

The Playwright Extension (`packages/extension`) is designed to let an MCP client (e.g. an AI
coding agent) drive an existing Chrome browser through the extension's relay. In practice, only
one such connection is supported at a time.

### Problem

Opening a second `--extension` connection while a first one is still active disconnects the first
connection and takes over the browser, instead of the two coexisting. This makes it impossible to
run more than one MCP client against the same browser profile at once — for example, two separate
agent instances (Claude Code, or any other MCP client) each trying to drive their own tabs in the
same browser.

Concretely, today: connection B arriving silently kicks out connection A mid-task, with no
indication to A's client that anything happened beyond its browser tools suddenly failing.

### To reproduce

1. Start an MCP client with `--extension --browser chrome` (client A), connect it to a tab.
2. While A is still connected, start a second MCP client the same way (client B), connect it to a
   different tab.
3. Client A's next tool call fails — its connection was torn down when B connected, even though A
   never disconnected and B targeted an unrelated tab.

### Proposed fix

I have a working fix (extension-side, `packages/extension/src/background.ts` and
`connectedTabGroup.ts`, plus the status page) that:

- Tracks connections in a map keyed by the connecting tab id, instead of a single active
  connection.
- Gives each connection its own Chrome tab group (`Playwright · <clientName>`, with a `(2)`, `(3)`
  ... suffix when connections share a client name), so a user can visually tell which tabs belong
  to which connection.
- Updates the status page to show one block per active connection, each independently
  disconnectable.

No protocol version bump needed, no change to `packages/playwright-core`'s server-side MCP tools.
Covered by a new test file (`tests/extension/multi-connection.spec.ts`), which passes locally.

I have this ready as a small, self-contained diff (extension-side only) and would like to open a
PR with it, per the contribution guidelines asking to check in here first. Happy to adjust the
approach based on feedback — let me know if this is a direction the team wants, or if a different
approach to multi-connection support is preferred.

### Steps to reproduce

Two MCP clients on one server with `--shared-browser-context`, both using the `devtools` caps.

```
npx @playwright/mcp --port 8931 --shared-browser-context --caps=devtools
```

1. Client A connects, navigates, calls `browser_start_recording`.
2. Client B connects, calls `browser_start_recording`.
3. Client A navigates (an action that should be recorded for A), then calls `browser_stop_recording`.
4. Client B navigates, then calls `browser_stop_recording`.

### Expected behavior

Either B's `browser_start_recording` is refused because a recording is already in progress on the
shared context, or the two recordings are kept separate. Whichever is chosen, A's actions should not
end up in B's transcript, and nobody should silently get an empty result.

### Actual behavior

A's action is handed to B, and A is told nothing was recorded:

```
A start  -> "Recording started. Call browser_stop_recording to retrieve the recorded actions."
B start  -> "Recording started. Call browser_stop_recording to retrieve the recorded actions."
A stop   -> "Recording stopped. No actions were recorded."
B stop   -> "Recording stopped. Recorded actions:
              await page.goto('http://localhost:8907/empty.html');"
```

That `goto` is **A's** navigation from step 3, not B's. So:

- B's start is not refused even though the shared context is already recording.
- A loses its recording entirely and is told "No actions were recorded", with no error.
- B receives an action performed by a different client.

### Additional context

`browser_start_recording` guards on per-`Context` state
(`packages/playwright-core/src/tools/backend/context.ts:241`):

```ts
async startRecording() {
  if (this._recordedActions)
    throw new Error('Recording is already in progress.');
```

but with `--shared-browser-context` each client gets its own `Context` while sharing one
`BrowserContext` object. `program.ts:137`:

```ts
const browserContext = config.browser.isolated ? await browser.newContext(config.browser.contextOptions) : browser.contexts()[0];
```

and the sink on the client `BrowserContext` is a single field, not a set
(`packages/playwright-core/src/client/browserContext.ts:88`, assigned at `:543`), so B's
`_enableRecorder` overwrites A's sink. A's later `stopRecording` then calls `_disableRecorder()` on
the shared context, which is why B's own recorder also stops.

Note `--isolated` is unaffected, since that branch gives each client its own `newContext()`. Only
`--shared-browser-context` shares the object.

Existing coverage: `tests/mcp/recorder.spec.ts` uses a single-client fixture, and "start twice" and
"stop without start" are tested and behave as asserted on one client. The two-client shared-context
interleaving is untested. `tests/mcp/http.spec.ts:394` already has a two-client shared-context
harness that this can be reproduced in with a few lines.

I have not opened a PR. Mine keep getting closed over an unsigned CLA on my side, so this is more
useful to you as a report, and the right fix here looks like a design call anyway (refuse the second
start versus make the sink per-client) rather than something I should pick for you.

I verified the transcript above by running it rather than reasoning from the source, since the
outcome surprised me: I expected B's result to be truncated, not to contain A's action. if I have
mischaracterised the intended behaviour of --shared-browser-context, happy to be corrected. freshman
in college, thanks for reading :)

gitCommitInfoPlugin hangs the whole run on pull_request CI when origin credentials are unavailable (git fetch blocks in GCM prompt on Windows service accounts)

## Summary

On GitHub Actions `pull_request` runs, when the workspace has no usable `origin` credentials (e.g. `actions/checkout` with `persist-credentials: false`), the whole Playwright run hangs indefinitely before printing `Running N tests`. The process stays idle: near-zero CPU, no test workers spawned, no TCP connections, until the job timeout kills it.

## Root cause

`lib/plugins/gitCommitInfoPlugin.js` → `gitDiff()`: when `ci.prBaseHash` is set (pull_request events only) and `captureGitInfo.diff` is enabled (the default in CI), it runs:

```
git fetch origin <base.sha> --depth=1 --no-auto-maintenance --no-auto-gc --no-tags --no-recurse-submodules
```

via `spawnAsync(command, [], { stdio: "pipe", shell: true, timeout: GIT_OPERATIONS_TIMEOUT_MS })` with `GIT_OPERATIONS_TIMEOUT_MS = 3000`.

Without origin credentials, that fetch invokes the credential helper (Git Credential Manager). On a Windows self-hosted runner running as a service (session 0, e.g. NETWORK SERVICE) the credential prompt never resolves, and the 3s spawn timeout does not terminate the `cmd → git → GCM` grandchild chain, so the returned promise never settles. This is inside the pre-collection `plugin setup` task, so the run stalls permanently.

Evidence from a live stall (GitHub Actions self-hosted Windows runner, `pull_request` event):

- `DEBUG=pw:test*` trace ends at `pw:test:task "plugin setup" started` (never finishes).
- Node diagnostic report at +300s: event loop idle, 5 pipe/socket handles (stdio + the hung child), 0 active requests.

All other trigger types (`workflow_dispatch`/`push`/`schedule`) are unaffected because `gitDiff` returns early when `ci.prBaseHash` is absent — the hang is 100% correlated with `pull_request` + missing origin credentials.

## Suggested fixes (any of)

1. Reap the process tree on timeout on Windows (e.g. `taskkill /T /F`) or hard-abandon the promise when the timeout fires.
2. Skip the fetch when the repo has no usable credentials / when `persist-credentials: false` can be detected (e.g. no `http.<url>.extraheader` and no credential helper configured).
3. Fail fast with a clear error instead of hanging (the current failure mode is silent and extremely hard to diagnose).

## Workaround

`captureGitInfo: { diff: false }` in the Playwright config disables the fetch entirely (commit info still works via local `git log`).

## Environment

- Playwright 1.5x (current), GitHub Actions, self-hosted Windows Server runner (NETWORK SERVICE, session 0), actions/checkout v6 with `persist-credentials: false`.

[MCP]: option to close the browser after an idle period

### What's going on?

Client is Claude Code, running the server over stdio as `npx @playwright/mcp@latest --headless --browser chromium`. chromium-1243, Node v22.22.3, Debian 13, 16 cores.

The server launches a browser on the first tool call and keeps it until the process exits. As far as I can tell there's no way to put a bound on that.

Usually that's fine. But if the last thing I did was navigate to a page with a running requestAnimationFrame loop, the browser just carries on rendering it. Headless chromium uses `--use-angle=swiftshader-webgl`, so a WebGL canvas gets rasterized on the CPU, and the gpu-process then sits at around 700% (13 raster threads) for as long as the server is up. I've had that go for 30 and for 90 minutes before I noticed, with load average up around 22 on a 16 core box.

I don't think it's a process leak. If I SIGTERM or SIGKILL the server the whole browser tree goes with it, both times I tried. The browser stays up because the server does, and a client will normally keep a stdio server running for the whole session.

The workaround is to call `browser_close`, but that leaves every client having to remember it every time, and closing at end of session is too late to help. `--timeout-action`, `--timeout-navigation` and `--timeout-settle` are all per operation, so none of them cover this.

Would you consider something like `--timeout-idle <ms>`, closing the browser after that long with no tool call and relaunching on the next one? The lazy launch already exists for the first call.

To reproduce:

1. Start `npx @playwright/mcp@latest --headless --browser chromium`.
2. `browser_navigate` to any page with a continuous WebGL rAF loop.
3. Stop issuing tool calls, leave the server up.
4. `ps -eo pid,pcpu,args --sort=-pcpu | grep '[m]s-playwright'`

[MCP]: switch between light and dark color scheme

### What's going on?

## Motivation

Coding agents driving the Playwright MCP server can only test a UI in whatever color scheme
the browser happened to start in. Frontend work almost always needs both — an agent that
implements or reviews a dark theme currently has no way to see it.

Nothing on the MCP surface exposes the color scheme today:

- None of the ~70 tools touches it (`browser_resize` is the closest neighbour).
- There is no CLI flag and no `PLAYWRIGHT_MCP_*` env var for it.

The existing workarounds are all unsuitable for an agent mid-session:

- `browser.contextOptions.colorScheme` in the JSON config file — requires writing a config
  file and restarting the server, and is fixed for the whole session.
- `--init-page` calling `page.emulateMedia({ colorScheme: 'dark' })` — same restart problem.
- `browser_run_code_unsafe` — arbitrary code execution, off by default for good reason, and
  not something an agent should reach for to flip a media query.

Playwright itself supports this fully via
[`page.emulateMedia()`](https://playwright.dev/docs/api/class-page#page-emulate-media) and
`contextOptions.colorScheme`, so this is purely about surfacing existing capability.

## Proposal

**1. A `browser_emulate_media` tool** wrapping `page.emulateMedia()`, with all parameters
optional so omitted media features are left unchanged:

| Parameter | Values |
|---|---|
| `colorScheme` | `light`, `dark` |
| `reducedMotion` | `reduce`, `no-preference` |
| `forcedColors` | `active`, `none` |
| `contrast` | `more`, `no-preference` |
| `media` | `screen`, `print` |

Scope matches `browser_resize`: `core` capability (available by default), applies to the
current page only, since `page.setViewportSize()` is per-page in exactly the same way.
Mirroring `emulateMedia` rather than adding a color-scheme-only tool means reduced-motion,
forced-colors and print emulation come along without a second tool later — useful for
accessibility and print-stylesheet testing.

**2. A `--color-scheme <light|dark>` CLI option** (plus `PLAYWRIGHT_MCP_COLOR_SCHEME`),
mapping to `contextOptions.colorScheme` alongside the existing `--viewport-size` and
`--user-agent` handling, so a whole session can be started in dark mode without a config
file.

## Example

```
browser_navigate      { "url": "http://localhost:3000" }
browser_take_screenshot
browser_emulate_media { "colorScheme": "dark" }
browser_take_screenshot
```

[MCP] Option for absolute paths in tool result links

Tool results name generated files with paths relative to the server's working directory, for example `- [Snapshot](./page-2026-08-25T09-14-22-104Z.yml)`.

A client that is not a process with a working directory cannot resolve these. This is the normal case when the consumer is a model rather than a shell.

It would cover the screenshot, PDF and storage-state links, the snapshot link, the console log link, the download line, binary response body lines, and the trace links. They all resolve through the same two call sites.

Page.content() omits shadow DOM, but locators pierce it — selectors that look unique silently aren't (revives #30816) ### Problem `Page.content()` only serializes light DOM — shadow root contents are invisible to it, which is expected per the DOM serialization spec. But Playwright's own CSS-based locators pierce open shadow roots by default when matching at runtime. That mismatch is a real footgun for anything that builds selectors or automation from `page.content()`'s output (scrapers, selector generators, AI browser agents, test recorders): a CSS path that looks unique in the light-DOM-only HTML can still match a *second* element inside an open shadow root — silently, since matching succeeds and no error is raised. The result is a click (or any locator action) landing on the wrong element, indistinguishable from a correct one. ### Minimal repro ```python html = """
""" page.set_content(html) # Looks unique in page.content() — the shadow button is invisible to it. assert page.content().count(" button").count() == 2 # not 1 ``` A tool that parses `page.content()`, sees one `

query:
[Bug]: transform cache ignores jsxImportSource, so .tsx specs fail after playwright moves to another path

### Version

1.63.0 (also 1.62.1)

### Steps to reproduce

```sh
mkdir repro && cd repro && mkdir tests
echo '{ "private": true, "devDependencies": { "@playwright/test": "1.63.0" } }' > package.json
printf "import { defineConfig } from '@playwright/test'\nexport default defineConfig({ testDir: './tests' })\n" > playwright.config.ts
printf "import { test, expect } from '@playwright/test'\nconst element = <div />\ntest('jsx', () => { expect(element).toBeTruthy() })\n" > tests/jsx.spec.tsx

npm install                          # hoisted layout: node_modules/playwright exists
npx playwright test --list           # 1 test, and the transformed spec is cached

rm -rf node_modules package-lock.json
pnpm install                         # isolated layout: playwright lives under node_modules/.pnpm
pnpm exec playwright test --list     # 0 tests
```

### Expected behavior

The spec is listed after the reinstall, as it is with an empty transform cache (`PWTEST_CACHE_DIR=$(mktemp -d) pnpm exec playwright test --list` lists 1 test).

### Actual behavior

```
Error: Cannot find module '<project>/node_modules/playwright/jsx-runtime'
Require stack:
- <project>/tests/jsx.spec.tsx
- <project>/node_modules/.pnpm/playwright@1.63.0/node_modules/playwright/lib/common/index.js
...
Error: No tests found
Total: 0 tests in 0 files
```

### Additional context

`configLoader.ts` compiles JSX with an absolute import source, `jsxImportSource = path.dirname(require.resolve('playwright'))`. But `calculateHash` in `transform/transform.ts` keys the cache on the content, file path, `version` and epilogue plugins only. So a cached `.tsx` transform keeps importing the old install path after `playwright` resolves somewhere else, even though its version is unchanged.

In practice this hits any reused checkout path whose install layout changes, for example a recreated git worktree, a switch between npm and pnpm, or a `node_modules` rebuilt by a newer package manager. The result is a silent collection of zero tests.

Including `jsxImportSource` (or the whole transform config) in the hash would fix it. #27285 looks like the earlier bare-specifier form of the same runtime lookup; this is its absolute-path counterpart.

### Environment

```
OS: macOS 26 (Darwin 25.6.0), arm64
Node.js: 26.8.1
npm 11, pnpm 11.10.0
```

query:
[Feature]: Failures-only terminal reporter (suppress passing test output)

### 🚀 Feature Request

Add a built-in way to suppress passing tests from terminal output entirely, so only failures (plus the final summary) are printed.

Today the closest options are:

- `--reporter=line`, which still prints a status line per test
- `--reporter=dot`, which still prints a character per test
- `list` with `printFailuresInline` (#40875), which prints failures as they happen but still prints one line per passing test

None of them get to "print nothing unless something failed."

Could equally be a `quiet`/`failuresOnly` option on the existing `list` reporter rather than a new reporter name.

### Example

```sh
npx playwright test --reporter=only-failures
```

```
  1) [chromium] › tests/checkout.spec.ts:42:3 › applies discount code

    Error: expect(received).toBe(expected)
    Expected: 1
    Received: 0

      44 |   await page.getByRole('button', { name: 'Apply' }).click();
    > 45 |   expect(await rows.count()).toBe(1);

  1 failed, 217 passed (1.2m)
```

Compared to today's `line` reporter on the same run, which prints 217 lines before the one that matters.

### Motivation

On a large suite most runs are green, and the per-test lines are pure noise. They push the thing you actually care about off the top of the scrollback, and in CI they inflate log size for no benefit. Scanning hundreds of lines to find the one `✘` is a worse experience than being shown only the failure.

This has become sharper with coding agents. A tool call that runs the test suite returns its entire stdout into the model's context window, so a green run of 500 tests spends thousands of tokens saying "everything is fine." That context is finite and shared with the actual source files the agent needs to hold onto. Piping through `grep` is lossy and fragile, since it drops the stack trace and code frame that make a failure diagnosable. An official failures-only mode means the run costs near-zero context when it passes and full detail when it doesn't, which is exactly the shape you want.

Prior art: Bun added `--only-failures` for exactly this, alongside its dots reporter. Jest has `jest-quiet-reporter` in userland for the same reason.

Bun also ships an `isAIAgent()` check that reads `AGENT=1` along with tool-specific variables, and Laravel Pint switches to `--format agent` when it detects `CLAUDECODE`, so tools adapting their output to agent context is an established pattern (see agentsmd/agents.md#136 for the push to standardize `AGENT=1` as the agent equivalent of `CI=true`). Playwright could eventually default to failures-only under that signal, though an explicit flag is the useful first step and is valuable on its own.

A custom reporter works, but this seems common enough to be worth having out of the box.

[Bug] Chromium: launch({ proxy: { username, password } }) credentials are sent to a website's 401 Basic challenge

## Version
- Playwright 1.62.0 (Python, `playwright` package; same code in playwright-core `coreBundle.js`)
- Chromium (bundled `chromium_headless_shell-1234`)
- macOS 26.5 (should be platform independent)

## Steps to reproduce
Fully local, self-contained script (no external network access): a Basic-auth HTTP proxy on 127.0.0.1 and a site that returns `401 WWW-Authenticate: Basic`.

```python
"""Minimal repro: Playwright launch proxy credentials are sent to a site's 401 Basic challenge.

Local only: a tiny HTTP proxy that requires Basic auth (127.0.0.1) and a site that answers 401 Basic.
"""
import asyncio
import base64
import threading
from http.server import BaseHTTPRequestHandler, ThreadingHTTPServer

import urllib.request

from playwright.async_api import async_playwright

PROXY_USER, PROXY_PASS = "proxyuser", "proxy-secret-123"
SEEN = []


class Site(BaseHTTPRequestHandler):
    def do_GET(self):
        SEEN.append((self.path, self.headers.get("Authorization")))
        if self.path.startswith("/protected"):
            self.send_response(401)
            self.send_header("WWW-Authenticate", 'Basic realm="site"')
            self.end_headers()
            self.wfile.write(b"no")
            return
        self.send_response(200)
        self.end_headers()
        self.wfile.write(b"ok")

    def log_message(self, *a):
        pass


class Proxy(BaseHTTPRequestHandler):
    def do_GET(self):
        want = "Basic " + base64.b64encode(f"{PROXY_USER}:{PROXY_PASS}".encode()).decode()
        if self.headers.get("Proxy-Authorization") != want:
            self.send_response(407)
            self.send_header("Proxy-Authenticate", 'Basic realm="proxy"')
            self.end_headers()
            return
        headers = {k: v for k, v in self.headers.items() if k.lower() not in ("proxy-authorization", "proxy-connection")}
        req = urllib.request.Request(self.path.replace("site.test", "127.0.0.1"), headers=headers)
        try:
            resp = urllib.request.urlopen(req)
            status, body, rh = resp.status, resp.read(), resp.headers
        except urllib.error.HTTPError as e:
            status, body, rh = e.code, e.read(), e.headers
        self.send_response(status)
        for k, v in rh.items():
            if k.lower() not in ("transfer-encoding", "connection"):
                self.send_header(k, v)
        self.end_headers()
        self.wfile.write(body)

    def log_message(self, *a):
        pass


def serve(handler):
    srv = ThreadingHTTPServer(("127.0.0.1", 0), handler)
    threading.Thread(target=srv.serve_forever, daemon=True).start()
    return srv


async def main():
    site, proxy = serve(Site), serve(Proxy)
    site_url = f"http://site.test:{site.server_port}"
    async with async_playwright() as p:
        browser = await p.chromium.launch(
            proxy={"server": f"http://127.0.0.1:{proxy.server_port}", "username": PROXY_USER, "password": PROXY_PASS},
            args=["--proxy-bypass-list=<-loopback>"],
        )
        page = await browser.new_page()
        r1 = await page.goto(site_url + "/warm")          # proxy auth happens here (cache becomes warm)
        r2 = await page.goto(site_url + "/protected")     # site answers 401 Basic
        print("warm status", r1.status, "| protected status", r2.status)
        await browser.close()
    leaked = [a for path, a in SEEN if path.startswith("/protected") and a]
    for path, a in SEEN:
        print("site saw", path, "Authorization:", (base64.b64decode(a.split()[1]).decode() if a else None))
    print("LEAK" if any(PROXY_PASS in base64.b64decode(a.split()[1]).decode() for a in leaked) else "NO LEAK")


asyncio.run(main())
```

Run: `pip install playwright && playwright install chromium && python repro.py`

## Expected
The proxy credentials are used only for the proxy's `407 Proxy-Authenticate` challenge. A site's `401 WWW-Authenticate` challenge should get no credentials (or only `httpCredentials` explicitly configured for that origin).

## Actual
The site receives `Authorization: Basic base64("proxyuser:proxy-secret-123")`:

```
warm status 200 | protected status 401
site saw /warm Authorization: None
site saw /protected Authorization: None
site saw /protected Authorization: proxyuser:proxy-secret-123   <-- proxy credentials sent to the website
```

## Cause (from reading the source)
1. `CRBrowserContext` constructor calls `authenticateProxyViaCredentials()`, which copies the launch proxy credentials into `this._options.httpCredentials = { username, password }` with **no `origin`**, overwriting any user-supplied `httpCredentials`.
2. `CRNetworkManager._onAuthRequired(event)` decides via `_shouldProvideCredentials(event.request.url)`. Without an `origin`, that returns true for every request, so it answers `Fetch.authRequired` with `ProvideCredentials` regardless of `event.authChallenge.source` (`"Proxy"` vs `"Server"`).

On a cold cache the single per-request attempt is consumed by the proxy's 407, so the site's 401 gets `CancelAuth`; once the proxy auth is cached, the site's 401 gets the proxy credentials.

## Things tried
- `new_context(http_credentials={..., "origin": <proxy origin>})` together with launch proxy credentials: overwritten by step 1, still leaks.
- Proxy credentials only via `http_credentials` with proxy origin (no launch credentials): the origin is compared against the request URL (the site), so the proxy's 407 is not answered.
- `extra_http_headers={"Proxy-Authorization": ...}`: for HTTPS this ends up inside the tunnel and is sent to the site, which is worse.

## Suggested fix
Keep proxy credentials separate from `httpCredentials`, and in `_onAuthRequired` use `event.authChallenge.source`: answer `"Proxy"` challenges only with the proxy credentials and `"Server"` challenges only with `httpCredentials` (subject to its `origin`). Firefox/WebKit backends may need the same check.

## Security note
Any website the automated browser visits can obtain the proxy credentials by returning `401 Basic`. For authenticated corporate/residential proxies this exposes the proxy account.

Agent host: support GitHub Enterprise (GHE) for Copilot auth

Today the agent host's Copilot auth path is hardcoded to github.com end-to-end. To use Copilot from a GHE instance, two layers need to change in lockstep:

## 1. Agent host: protected-resource metadata is github.com-only

The Copilot agent's `getProtectedResources()` only advertises github.com:

```ts
getProtectedResources(): ProtectedResourceMetadata[] {
    return [{
        resource: 'https://api.github.com',
        resource_name: 'GitHub Copilot',
        authorization_servers: ['https://github.com/login/oauth'],
        scopes_supported: ['read:user', 'user:email'],
        required: true,
    }];
}
```

This drives which OAuth server the CLI / client performs the device-code flow against. For a GHE user it needs to advertise `https://<ghe-host>/api/v3` (or equivalent) and `https://<ghe-host>/login/oauth`. The GHE host should be **configurable by the agent host operator** (config file / env / launch flag) so a single agent-host binary can be pointed at any GHE instance without a rebuild.

## 2. `CopilotApiService`: token mint URL is hardcoded to `defaultChatAgent.tokenEntitlementUrl`

See the TODO in `src/vs/platform/agentHost/node/shared/copilotApiService.ts` (`_buildCapiInit`):

```ts
// TODO(GHE): For GitHub Enterprise users the mint URL must point to
// `api.<enterprise-host>/copilot_internal/v2/token` instead.
const tokenUrl = this._productService.defaultChatAgent.tokenEntitlementUrl;
```

For GHE this needs to point at `api.<ghe-host>/copilot_internal/v2/token` instead of `api.github.com/...`. The enterprise host has to thread through the public `ICopilotApiService` surface (extra param on `messages`/`models`, a per-host instance, or a `create(enterpriseHost?)` factory) — `defaultAccount.ts` in the workbench already derives this URL the same way for the main auth path and is a good reference.

## Why this is one issue

(1) and (2) are coupled — fixing only the mint URL doesn't help if the OAuth flow still hits github.com, and vice versa. Both should land together with a shared "GHE host" configuration source.

## Out of scope

- The Copilot CLI's own OAuth handling (Rust, in `cli/`) is github.com-hardcoded but is a separate consumer; this issue is specifically about the agent host being usable against a GHE Copilot.

query:
Editor type dropdown in the breadcrumbs bar to switch/set the editor for a file

### Problem

When a file can be opened by more than one editor (for example a `*.md` file that can open in the text editor, the Markdown preview, or the Markdown editor), there is no obvious, always-visible way to see which editor is currently used or to switch to another one. Today users have to know about the `Reopen Editor With…` command, and there is no affordance in the editor chrome that surfaces the available editors.

This is especially relevant now that custom editors opt out of diffs/merges by default (#324791): users may want to quickly switch a diff between the text diff editor and a custom diff editor, or set a per-extension default.

### Proposal

Add a small dropdown on the right-hand side of the **breadcrumbs bar** that shows the current editor type as text (for example "Markdown Preview", "Text Editor", or "Text Diff Editor" in a diff) and, when clicked, opens a menu to:

- **Switch** the active editor to any of the other editors that can open the resource (reuses `reopenActiveEditorWith`). The current editor is checked.
- **Set Default** for the file type via a submenu. In a diff context this writes to `workbench.diffEditorAssociations`; otherwise to `workbench.editorAssociations`. The currently configured default is checked.
- In a diff, **Open Original** / **Open Modified** as standalone editors.

Details:

- The dropdown only appears when a **more specialized editor is available** — i.e. more than one editor can open the resource. It is hidden for plain text files (only the default editor) and for exclusive editors such as the Hex editor (which return no alternatives).
- Extension-provided editors show their source (`Label - Extension Name`); built-in editors show just their label.
- In a diff context, the default text editor is labeled "Text Diff Editor" to match how it actually opens.
- Only shown on the dedicated breadcrumbs bar (tabbed mode), not the inline single-tab breadcrumbs.
- Behind an experimental setting `breadcrumbs.showEditorType` (default `true`).

### Verification steps

1. Ensure a file type has multiple editors (e.g. Markdown: text editor + Markdown preview). Open a `*.md` file.
2. The breadcrumbs bar shows a dropdown on the right with the current editor type (e.g. "Text Editor").
3. Click it → menu lists the available editors with the current one checked; picking another reopens the file with it.
4. Use the **Set Default** submenu → the chosen editor is written to `workbench.editorAssociations` for `*.md` and becomes the default.
5. Open a `*.md` diff → the dropdown shows "Text Diff Editor"; the **Set Default (Diff Only)** submenu writes to `workbench.diffEditorAssociations`; **Open Original** / **Open Modified** open each side.
6. Open a plain `*.txt` file (only the default editor) or a file handled by an exclusive editor (Hex) → the dropdown is hidden.
7. Set `"breadcrumbs.showEditorType": false` → the dropdown disappears; set it back to `true` → it returns.

Agents window: corrupted session file silently loads as empty instead of surfacing error

## Bug Description

When opening an old session in the Agents window, if the Copilot SDK rejects `session.resume` due to a validation error in the session file, the agent host silently falls back to `createSession` with the same ID. This results in the session appearing to load successfully but showing **0 turns** — all conversation history is lost without any user-facing error.

## Steps to Reproduce

1. Have an existing agent session with conversation history
2. The session file becomes corrupted (in this case, a compaction metadata field fails validation)
3. Open the session in the Agents window
4. Session appears empty — no error shown to user

## Expected Behavior

The user should be informed that the session could not be restored due to corruption, rather than silently presenting an empty session.

## Actual Behavior

The session loads with 0 turns. The user sees a blank conversation with no indication that data was lost.

## Relevant Logs

```
[Copilot:df7c418f-...] _resumeSession called — session not in memory, resuming...
[Copilot:df7c418f-...] Calling SDK resumeSession...
[Copilot:df7c418f-...] SDK resumeSession failed: code=-32603, message=Request session.resume failed with message: Session file is corrupted (line 19567: data.compactionTokensUsed.copilotUsage.tokenDetails.0.batchSize: Number must be greater than 0)
[Copilot:df7c418f-...] Resume failed (code=-32603), falling back to createSession with same ID
[Copilot:df7c418f-...] Fallback createSession succeeded
[AgentHostStateManager] Restored session: copilotcli:/df7c418f-... (0 turns)
[AgentService] Restored session copilotcli:/df7c418f-... with 0 turns
```

## Analysis

The fallback logic is in `src/vs/platform/agentHost/node/copilot/copilotAgent.ts` around line 1626:

```typescript
if (!err || errCode !== -32603) {
    throw err;
}
// Falls back to createSession with same ID
```

The comment says _"The SDK fails to resume sessions that have no messages"_ — but error code `-32603` is also returned for **data corruption**, not just empty sessions. The fallback does not distinguish between these cases.

## Suggested Fix

Two potential approaches:
1. **Agent Host**: Parse the error message to distinguish "no messages" from "corrupted" — surface a notification to the user when data is actually corrupted rather than silently creating an empty session
2. **SDK**: The validation on `batchSize > 0` in compaction metadata should not prevent loading the actual conversation turns — this is metadata, not content

* Custom Endpoint BYOK /responses: next-turn request remains unexpectedly large
* BYOK chat-completions : next-turn request becomes compact as expected

# Steps to Reproduce
1. Configure a BYOK Custom Endpoint that uses the Responses API (/responses).
2. Start a conversation long enough to trigger compaction / summarization.

* previous_response_id is present
* the request succeeds
* but the request still contains a large serialized local history payload

After compaction, when a valid previous_response_id is available, the next request should send only the minimal continuation history required by the Responses API, plus any necessary compaction round-trip item.

That is the behavior I observed with chat-completions BYOK, and what I expected from the /responses BYOK path as well.

On Custom Endpoint /responses BYOK, the next request includes previous_response_id, but also re-sends a large local serialized history blob.

I captured the failing request at my upstream gateway. The large serialized local history was already present before the request was forwarded upstream. That rules out the gateway as the origin of the oversized payload.

That suggests the next request should shrink when continuation state is available.

I am not attaching raw logs because they contain private conversation contents, local paths, shell history, endpoint/provider metadata, and request identifiers.

The important part is:

It can also export the captured request as raw HTTP, JSON, Markdown, or HAR, which may make it easier to attach a redacted repro without publishing the full conversation.
> 
> This is diagnostic rather than a workaround, but it should produce a compact artifact showing whether the duplication originates in VS Code's local history serialization or in the downstream gateway.
> 
> Project: https://github.com/jianshuo/ccglass
> ```

After some more experiments. I've found the issue. This setting needs to be turned on:
GitHub › Copilot › Chat › Responses Api Context Management

Also, Bifrost is dropping context-management params. After fixing it and enabling the setting, compaction works.

Note: This does not mean that there isn't a bug with VSCode compaction with BYOK in /responses. This just means that there is a workaround and it is to enable GitHub › Copilot › Chat › Responses Api Context Management

query:
Duplicate Copilot telemetry event names produce different schemas from identical source

## Problem

The Copilot extension contains multiple `__GDPR__` declarations for the same telemetry event names, with different metadata and property schemas. The generated telemetry contract is therefore ambiguous even though all producers emit under the same event name.

### `languageModelToolInvoked`

The [Claude Code path](https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/blob/f80f16c92ce08e7f53609f359e92434c84565c4b/extensions/copilot/src/extension/chatSessions/claude/common/claudeMessageDispatch.ts#L446) declares:

```ts
"languageModelToolInvoked": {
    "owner": "roblourens",
    "comment": "Provides insight into the usage of language model tools (Claude Code agent).",
    "toolId": { ..., "comment": "The Claude Code SDK tool name (e.g. Bash, Read, Edit, mcp__server__tool)." },
    "toolExtensionId": { ..., "comment": "Always undefined for Claude Code." },
    "toolSourceKind": { ..., "comment": "claudeCode | mcp" },
    ...
}
```

The [Copilot CLI path](https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/blob/f80f16c92ce08e7f53609f359e92434c84565c4b/extensions/copilot/src/extension/chatSessions/copilotcli/node/copilotcliSession.ts#L3162) independently declares the same event name:

```ts
"languageModelToolInvoked": {
    "owner": "roblourens",
    "comment": "Provides insight into the usage of language model tools (Copilot CLI agent).",
    "toolId": { ..., "comment": "The CLI/SDK tool name (e.g. bash, str_replace_editor, apply_patch)." },
    "toolExtensionId": { ..., "comment": "Always undefined for CLI." },
    "toolSourceKind": { ..., "comment": "copilotCli | mcp" },
    ...
}
```

### `summarizedConversationHistory`

The [foreground summarization path](https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/blob/f80f16c92ce08e7f53609f359e92434c84565c4b/extensions/copilot/src/extension/prompts/node/agent/summarizedConversationHistory.tsx#L1159) declares:

```ts
"summarizedConversationHistory": {
    "owner": "roblourens",
    "comment": "Tracks when summarization happens and what the outcome was",
    "summarizationId": { ... },
    "detailedOutcome": { ... },
    "numRoundsSinceLastSummarization": { ... },
    "hasWorkingNotebook": { ... },
    "mode": { ... },
    ...
}
```

The [background summarization path](https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/blob/f80f16c92ce08e7f53609f359e92434c84565c4b/extensions/copilot/src/extension/intents/node/agentIntent.ts#L1295) independently declares the same event name:

```ts
"summarizedConversationHistory": {
    "owner": "bhavyau",
    "comment": "Tracks background summarization outcome",
    "outcome": { ... },
    "model": { ... },
    "summarizationMode": { ... },
    ...
}
```

There is also a third declaration for the background-failure path in the same file.

## How the bug manifests

Azure Product runs [441170](https://dev.azure.com/monacotools/Monaco/_build/results?buildId=441170) and [441169](https://dev.azure.com/monacotools/Monaco/_build/results?buildId=441169) used the same VS Code commit, branch, pipeline revision, and parameters:

```text
commit: 2f243e3868ce88abcdea88ff2061b507a0f4a3fa
branch: refs/heads/hediet/b/low-lobster
```

Nevertheless, their generated `copilot-chat.vsix/extension/telemetry.json` schemas differ. One build retained the Claude Code declaration while the other retained the Copilot CLI declaration:

```text
"Always undefined for Claude Code." -> "Always undefined for CLI."
"claudeCode | mcp" -> "copilotCli | mcp"
```

For `summarizedConversationHistory`, the selected declaration changed from `owner: "roblourens"` to `owner: "bhavyau"`; fields including `summarizationId`, `detailedOutcome`, `hasWorkingNotebook`, `mode`, and `numRoundsSinceLastSummarization` were present in one generated schema and absent in the other.

This means repeated builds of identical source can produce different `telemetry.json` files, and the generated schema may describe only one producer even though multiple producers emit under the same event name.

## Expected

Each telemetry event name should have one authoritative declaration. Semantically different events should either use distinct names, or all emitters should share one declaration containing the intended schema. Repeated builds of one source revision should produce the same telemetry contract.

Allow disabling or hiding MCP servers registered by extensions

Problem

MCP servers that are added by extensions show up under "Chat: Open Customizations" → MCP Servers and are starting automatically or when interacting with the Chat features. I have multiple extension-provided MCP servers that I never use; they pollute my server list and cause server-start operations to run indefinitely.

Reproduction

1. Install extensions that register MCP servers (e.g. extension(s) that add custom MCP servers).
2. Open the Command Palette → "Chat: Open Customizations" → MCP Servers.
3. Observe that extension-provided MCP servers appear in the list.
4. Attempting to disable servers only works for user-provided servers; extension-provided servers have no obvious "Disable" action.

Current workaround

The UI allows disabling only user-provided MCP servers (right-click → "Disable"). Extension-provided servers cannot be disabled via the same discoverable UI.

Request

Please add a way to disable or hide MCP servers that are registered by extensions. Suggested approaches:

- Allow disabling/hiding extension-provided MCP servers from the MCP Servers list (right-click → "Disable" for extension servers as well).
- Show the source extension for each MCP server and provide an affordance to toggle it per-server (and/or link to the contributing extension's settings).
- Add a setting to prevent automatic starting of extension-provided MCP servers (e.g., "mcp.servers.startOnDemand": true/false) or a per-server opt-out.

Why this matters

- Reduces noise in the MCP Servers list for users who have many extensions that register servers they don't use.
- Prevents unnecessary or long-running server-start operations triggered by these servers.
- Makes it easier to manage which servers actually start and appear in chat context.

Notes / Context

- From a Slack thread: only user-provided MCP servers can currently be disabled; extension-provided servers appear undiscoverable and cannot be disabled.
- Affected user: connor4312 (reported having multiple unused servers starting infinitely).

Please consider adding either a per-server disable/hide action for extension-registered MCP servers, or a global setting to ignore or start them on demand.

Copilot run_in_terminal sandbox dependency installer is hardcoded to apt, breaks on Arch/Linux non-Debian distros

### Context
Using Copilot Chat terminal tools on Arch Linux with sandboxed execution enabled.

### Problem
When the terminal tool enters the sandbox dependency install/remediation flow, it attempts to run:

`sudo apt install -y <deps>`

On Arch (and other non-Debian distros), this fails because `apt` is not available. The user-facing result is:

`Sandbox dependency installation failed (exit code ...). The command was not executed.`

### Repro
1. On Arch Linux, ensure `bwrap` and `socat` are installed (for example via `pacman`).
2. Use Copilot Chat terminal tool (`run_in_terminal`) with sandboxed execution flow enabled.
3. Trigger a path that invokes missing dependency installation/remediation.
4. Observe attempted use of `apt` and failure.

### Expected
Dependency installation/remediation should be distro-aware (e.g. `pacman` on Arch, `dnf` on Fedora, `zypper` on openSUSE, etc.), or avoid shelling out to distro package managers directly and instead provide actionable instructions.

### Actual
Installer command is hardcoded to `apt`.

### Source reference
In `src/vs/workbench/contrib/terminalContrib/chatAgentTools/common/terminalSandboxService.ts`, `installMissingSandboxDependencies(...)` currently uses:

`sudo apt install -y ${depsList}`

This appears to be the root cause for Linux distro mismatch.

### Suggestion
- Detect distro/package manager at runtime and choose appropriate command.
- If unsupported/unknown distro, surface a targeted prompt with a copyable command suggestion instead of assuming `apt`.
- Optionally allow a configurable package install command for enterprise/custom environments.

Thanks!

Extend built-in on-device dictation to editor dictation, terminal voice, and add read-aloud (TTS)

### Summary

Now that VS Code has a built-in on-device dictation engine (`ILocalTranscriptionService`, gated by `chat.speechToText.enabled` / `chatSpeechToTextConfigured`), we should extend it to cover the remaining speech surfaces that today only work through the `ms-vscode.vscode-speech` extension. Doing so lets built-in speech fully supersede the extension for dictation + read-aloud, so we can retire the "disable the redundant Speech extension" prompt entirely.

Related: we've already made the built-in chat mic win over the extension mic (single mic icon) and gated the extension's chat keybinding. The extension still uniquely provides the surfaces below.

### Scope

Extend the built-in on-device engine to power:

- [ ] **Editor dictation** — `src/vs/workbench/contrib/codeEditor/browser/dictation/editorDictation.ts` (currently gated on `HasSpeechProvider`, uses the extension's `ISpeechService`). Route it through `ILocalTranscriptionService` when built-in dictation is configured.
- [ ] **Terminal voice dictation** — `src/vs/workbench/contrib/terminalContrib/voice/browser/terminalVoice.ts` / `terminalVoiceActions.ts`. Same: use the built-in engine when available.
- [ ] **Read aloud / text-to-speech** — the extension is the only provider of `ITextToSpeechSession` (`src/vs/workbench/contrib/speech/common/speechService.ts`). Built-in has no TTS today. Add an on-device (or platform) TTS path so "Read Aloud" in chat works without the extension.

### Motivation

- Built-in on-device speech is private (no audio leaves the machine) and ships in the box.
- Once these three surfaces are covered, `ms-vscode.vscode-speech` becomes fully redundant for dictation and read-aloud, so the redundant-extension notification can be removed rather than asking users to disable a still-useful extension.
- Consistent UX: one speech stack, one set of keybindings, no double mic / keybinding collisions.

Agents window hangs with per-group editor limit of 1

## Summary

The Agents window can enter an infinite editor open/close loop when the editor limit is enabled per group with a value of 1. The renderer main thread remains busy and the UI hangs.

## Configuration

```json
"workbench.editor.limit.perEditorGroup": true,
"workbench.editor.limit.value": 1,
"workbench.editor.limit.enabled": true
```

## Steps to reproduce

1. Apply the settings above.
2. Open the Agents window.
3. Open a workspace-backed session that uses the single-pane layout and has the managed Changes and Files tabs.

## Actual behavior

The UI hangs. The managed Changes and Files tabs continuously displace one another:

1. `SinglePaneManagedTabsStrategy` ensures both managed tabs.
2. Opening the second tab triggers `EditorsObserver.ensureOpenedEditorsLimit`, which evicts the least-recent tab because the per-group limit is 1.
3. The managed-tab editor-change observer sees the missing tab and reopens it.
4. The editor limit evicts the other managed tab, and the cycle repeats indefinitely.

## Expected behavior

The managed-tab reconciliation and editor-limit enforcement should reach a stable state. Enabling an editor limit of 1 must not cause an infinite open/close loop or hang the renderer.

## Trace evidence

- Renderer PID 20337 entered a `RunTask` at 9.185832 seconds after a mouse-release/session-open action.
- The task was still unfinished when the 71.9-second trace ended, after remaining open for at least 62.733 seconds.
- CPU samples repeatedly alternate between:
  - `SinglePaneManagedTabsStrategy._reconcileCore -> _openChangesTab/_openFilesTab`
  - `EditorsObserver.ensureOpenedEditorsLimit -> doEnsureOpenedEditorsLimit -> closeEditors`
- The renderer main thread is effectively continuously active from approximately 9.3 seconds onward.

## Introducing commit

`5cfa71584e11bc0fe673686a9306c285fb4956cd` — sessions: refine the single-pane detail-panel layout (#324348)

That commit first introduced the auto-managed Changes and Files tabs together with reconciliation on editor changes. Its parent does not contain the managed Files-tab reconciler; subsequent refactors preserve the conflicting invariant.

Agent Host terminal auto-approve should use PowerShell grammar for PowerShell commands

Follow up to #326766 and #324136. PR #327947 adds persistent user/workspace auto-approve actions to Agent Host Copilot terminal confirmations, but there is still a parser mismatch for the SDK's `powershell` tool.

The workbench generates suggestions using the PowerShell tree-sitter grammar, while Agent Host's `commandAutoApprover.ts` only loads `tree-sitter-bash.wasm` for eligibility and enforcement.

Impact:

- **Existing settings rule:** a simple rule such as `"Get-ChildItem": true` usually works because bash can treat it as a generic command name. Rules for PowerShell-specific syntax can still miss because Agent Host splits/interprets the command using bash grammar.
- **Rule added from #327947:** the workbench can suggest and persist a rule from an accurate PowerShell parse, but Agent Host re-parses the next command as bash. The user selects "Always Allow" and is prompted again.
- **Exact command-line rule:** this can also miss when bash parsing fails because Agent Host parses before checking the exact command-line allow rule.

Representative cases include pipelines with script blocks (`Where-Object { ... }`), `$()` subexpressions, backtick continuations, PowerShell operators, and PowerShell-specific redirects such as `$null`.

The expected failure mode is conservative re-prompting/inconsistent suggestions; Agent Host remains authoritative for approval. There is no known auto-approval bypass from this mismatch.

Work needed:

- Load `tree-sitter-powershell.wasm` in the Agent Host command auto-approver (it already ships in the same package).
- Carry/select the shell grammar for both rule eligibility and enforcement.
- Add coverage for existing settings rules and rules created from #327947, including PowerShell-specific sub-command and exact-command-line cases.

> Nemotron **(default)** - `nemotron-3.5-asr-streaming-0.6b`. Multilingual (35+ languages, auto-detected). [...] Verify it transcribes in that language without any language setting.

In 1.131 the default became `nemotron-speech-streaming-en-0.6b`, and the `dictation.model` enum only offers that one plus `mai`, so the multilingual model can no longer be selected. There is also a migration that rewrites the multilingual id back to the English one, so users who had it configured lose it.

I see that in your `foundry.modelinfo.json` it is already available as `nemotron-3.5-asr-streaming-0.6b`, so it can just be used again.

You also need to add the language the model will work with. Only switching the model is not enough: if I set `dictation.model` to the multilingual one by hand it does work, but without an explicit language it runs in auto-detect mode and on short phrases it keeps guessing English and transliterates instead (`privet` instead of `привет`).

You can get the list of languages for the config from here:
https://docs.nvidia.com/nim/speech/latest/reference/support-matrix/asr.html#asr-nemotron-asr-streaming-supported-languages
